issues.failure_explanation: By (C_t1), \|\phi^{j+1}-\phi^j\|_{H^1}\le C\|d_j\|_{H^1}, i.e. linear in \|d_j\|, not quadratic. The induction that keeps the iterates inside \mathcal{B}_{\sigma_2}(\widetilde\phi_g) therefore uses an invalid bound; the sum should be of \sqrt{C_\tau(1-2C_\tau(\mu-\varepsilon))^{j}\sigma_3}, giving a bound of order \sigma+C\sqrt{\sigma_3}/(1-\sqrt{1-2C_\tau(\mu-\varepsilon)}) rather than \sigma+C\sigma_3/(2(\mu-\varepsilon)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \|d_j\|^2 by \|d_j\| in the increment bound, sum the resulting geometric series of square roots, and choose \sigma,\sigma_3 so that \sigma+C\sqrt{\sigma_3}/(1-\sqrt{1-2C_\tau(\mu-\varepsilon)})<\sigma_2.
issues.overall_effect: The confinement argument (and hence the local convergence proof) is not correct as written; the conclusion remains attainable since the corrected geometric sum is still small for small \sigma_3.
issues.title: Induction step in proof of Theorem Local-Convergence bounds the increment by the squared gradient norm
issues.why_classification: A short local recomputation restores the induction with no change to the theorem's rate, constants type, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore,  reducing $\sigma_0$ appropriately, one can achieve a P-RG with superlinear local  convergence rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims superlinear local convergence is attainable. What is proved (Theorems Local-Convergence and Var-P-convergence) is a linear rate \sqrt{1-(\mu-\varepsilon)/(L+\varepsilon)} or (L-\mu)/(L+\mu)+\varepsilon with constants C_\varepsilon,\sigma depending on \varepsilon and on the fixed preconditioner; for the optimal preconditioner \mu<1=L for every fixed \sigma_0>0, and as \sigma_0\to0 the coercivity constant of \mathcal{P}_\phi degenerates (A6-(ii) constant, neighborhood size and C_\varepsilon are not shown uniform in \sigma_0). Nothing establishes a rate that decays faster than any geometric sequence; only arbitrarily small (but fixed) linear rates with uncontrolled constants follow.

failure_location.quote: Notably, a superlinear convergence rate (see \cite{2006Numerical}) is attainable when $\mu = L$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the superlinear claims and state only that the linear rate constant can be made arbitrarily close to 0 for fixed \sigma_0 (or \mu=L), with constants depending on \sigma_0/\varepsilon.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised superlinear guarantee (text after Theorem Local-Convergence and in the Conclusion) is not supported by any result in the paper.
issues.title: Unsupported claim of superlinear convergence (when \mu=L or by reducing \sigma_0)
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws a stated guarantee of a stronger convergence type; the core linear-rate theorems are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, it is not necessarily coercive even at $\phi_g$. Thus, a natural idea is to choose an optimal local preconditioner:

Since the optimal local preconditioner does not satisfy {\bf (A6)}-$(iii)$, its global convergence cannot be guaranteed in general. However, it can be shown that the optimal local preconditioner is Lipschitz continuous with respect to $\phi$

issues.failure_explanation: The whole framework (inner product (\cdot,\cdot)_{\mathcal P_\phi}, projection (Proj-P), Lemmas Polyak-Loj, C_t, G-spectrum, Theorem Local-Convergence) requires \mathcal P_\phi to be symmetric and coercive on all of H_0^1(\mathcal D) (A6-(ii)). For (Varep-P) the paper only addresses the degeneracy on T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M by the shift \sigma_0>0. But E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal I is guaranteed nonnegative only on T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M (second-order necessary condition); on span\{\phi_g\} and its couplings with the tangent space (e.g. \langle(E''(\phi_g)-\lambda_g\mathcal I)\phi_g,v\rangle=2(f'(\rho_{\phi_g})\rho_{\phi_g}\phi_g,v)_{L^2}) no sign or coercivity is established under (A1)-(A5), and a small \sigma_0 cannot compensate an indefinite direction. The paper only discusses Lipschitz continuity (replacing A6-(iii)); coercivity (and thus that \|\cdot\|_{\mathcal P_\phi} is a norm and \mathcal P_\phi^{-1} exists with the required bounds) is never verified for this preconditioner.

failure_location.quote: generated by the P-RG with the optimal local preconditioner \eqref{Varep-P} yields another locally linear convergence rate

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove coercivity of E''(\phi)-(\widetilde\lambda_\phi-\sigma_0)\mathcal I on H_0^1 near \phi_g (e.g. under an added assumption such as f'\ge0 plus an argument on span\{\phi_g\}\oplus T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M), or modify the preconditioner off the tangent space (e.g. add a rank-one term c\,\mathcal I\phi(\phi,\cdot)_{L^2}), verifying that the spectral quantities \mu, L and the identities \mathcal P_{\phi_g}^{-1}\mathcal I i\phi_g=i\phi_g/\sigma_0 etc. are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem Var-P-convergence (and Corollary E-eq-Phi when used with (Varep-P)) rests on an unverified hypothesis; if coercivity fails, the P-RG with (Varep-P) is not a Riemannian gradient method in the paper's sense and the local rate is unsupported.
issues.title: Optimal local preconditioner (Varep-P) is not shown to be coercive (A6-(ii)), yet Theorem Var-P applies the P-RG framework to it
issues.why_classification: A contained verification or a modified construction is needed; the rate (L-\mu)/(L+\mu) and the method survive, but not without a new argument or hypothesis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the second-order sufficient condition holds at the minimizer (e.g., when $\Omega=0$), then the operator $\mathcal{G}_{\tau}(\phi_g)$ can be analyzed over the entire tangent space, and the best convergence rate for gradient descent (cf.~{\bf Theorem~\ref{Var-P-convergence}}) extends to any preconditioner satisfying~\textbf{(A6)}.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition Property-P-(i) defines L as the supremum of the Rayleigh quotient over N_{\phi_g}\mathcal M (the L^2-orthogonal complement of T_{\phi_g}\mathcal S in the tangent space). The proof of Lemma C_t applies it to Proj^{\mathcal P_{\phi_g}}_{\phi_g}d_n, which lies in T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M but not in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal M in general (for generic \mathcal P, e.g. \mathcal H_0 or \mathcal H_\phi, the direction \mathcal P^{-1}(E''-\lambda_g\mathcal I)w has nonzero L^2-components along i\phi_g, i\mathcal L_z\phi_g). For v=v_N+v_S with v_N\in N, v_S\in T\mathcal S, one has \langle(E''-\lambda_g)v,v\rangle=\langle(E''-\lambda_g)v_N,v_N\rangle while \|v\|^2_{\mathcal P}=\|v_N\|^2_{\mathcal P}+2(v_N,v_S)_{\mathcal P}+\|v_S\|^2_{\mathcal P} can be smaller than \|v_N\|^2_{\mathcal P} when N is not \mathcal P-orthogonal to T\mathcal S; hence the supremum over T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M, L_T, generally exceeds L, and the claimed inequality with L is unjustified. Only for preconditioners with N\perp_{\mathcal P}T\mathcal S (such as (Varep-P), where L_T=L=1) does the step hold.

failure_location.quote: Using {\bf Proposition \ref{Property-P}}-$(i)$, the following upper bound estimate holds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine L in Lemma C_t and Theorem Local-Convergence as the supremum of the Rayleigh quotient over T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M (equivalently over the \mathcal P_{\phi_g}-orthogonal complement of T_{\phi_g}\mathcal S in the tangent space), or prove that the iteration directions asymptotically lie in N_{\phi_g}\mathcal M for the given preconditioner; note this gives a possibly worse rate for \mathcal P_1-\mathcal P_3 and requires recomputing L in the numerical table.
issues.overall_effect: The exact energy-dissipation constant C_\tau=\tau-\tau^2(L+\varepsilon)/2 and hence the rate \sqrt{1-(\mu-\varepsilon)/(L+\varepsilon)} and step-size range (0,2/(L+\varepsilon)) in Theorem Local-Convergence are not established with L as defined in (Mu-L) for general preconditioners satisfying (A6); Theorem Var-P-convergence is unaffected since there the two suprema coincide.
issues.title: Lemma C_t applies the upper spectral bound L (defined on N_{\phi_g}\mathcal M) to directions d_n that only lie in T_{\phi_g}\mathcal M
issues.why_classification: The result survives with a redefined (larger) constant L, a limited weakening that leaves a recognizably comparable rate; the optimal-preconditioner theorem is untouched.
